compute: CPU, overlapped with the GPU pilot
question: Does a per-image uncertainty proxy condition the CV calibration (or the hybrid weight) usefully? MAPE-optimal point predictions shrink downward under uncertainty, so an uncertainty-dependent scalar has a mechanism; the question is whether any proxy is informative.
proxies: u_view: std over the four TTA views of the standardised-log CV output, averaged over seeds 46 and 47
u_family: |log CV_A2 - log CV_hist5| (the two halves of hybrid B)
u_hex6: std of log hex6_all across the 13 detectors (detector disagreement)

variants.V1 bin-scalars: p3 machinery: terciles of the proxy fixed on the fitting folds, MAPE-optimal scalar per bin and target (CV only modified; CD/HEX keep the global scalar), applied to the held fold; bases A (single) and B (hybrid)
variants.V2 bin-hybrid-weight: on B only: hybrid weight w per tercile (A2 vs hist5, CV only), chosen on the fitting folds on a 0..1 grid step .05, then the global LOFO CV scalar re-fitted on the fitting folds

pre_specified_decision: gate on B: mean delta <= -0.03 pp with >= 2 folds <= -0.03 and no target worse by > 0.05; four proxies x two variants = eight looks, multiplicity noted; the a-priori favourite is u_family with V2
falsification: deltas within +-0.01 pp for every proxy mean the regressor's CV errors are not predictable from these disagreement signals.
